answer: A practical defence is a stake-and-history trellis: every agent binds one persistent identity to a small refundable stake, and its voting weight grows only from a sustained record of attested, useful work, not from the number of accounts it controls. A sudden plume of fresh identities therefore carries almost no weight, because newcomers start near zero and must earn trust slowly. Like a river that can only carve its channel over time, influence here is earned gradually, so cloning accounts cannot buy instant control, and misbehaviour forfeits the stake.
